A '''''Star Wars'' film series''' was announced by [[Lucasfilm]] in [[2018]] with [[David Benioff]] and [[D.B. Weiss]], the creators and showrunners of [[Wikipedia:HBO|HBO's]] [[Wikipedia:Game of Thrones (TV series)|''Game of Thrones'']], set to write and produce entries in the series, with the first film originally planned to release on [[December 16]], [[2022]]. However, in [[2019]], Benioff and Weiss departed the project. The first film's release slot was eventually given to the film [[Rogue Squadron (film)|''Rogue Squadron'']]. On [[January 10]], [[2024]], Benioff and Weiss confirmed in an interview with [[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''THR'']] that Lucasfilm ultimately passed on the project.

==Development==
Prior to the announcement of the film series, ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]] visited the set of [[Wikipedia:Game of Thrones (TV series)|''Game of Thrones'']]'s [[Wikipedia:Game of Thrones (season 8)|eighth and final season]] to give advice to writers [[David Benioff]] and [[D.B. Weiss]].<ref name="George S8">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/2019/04/01/george-lucas-game-of-thrones-season-8|text=George Lucas secretly visited the Game of Thrones season 8 set|author=James Hibberd|date=2019-04-01|work=[[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']]|archivedate=20190704043758}}</ref> The film series was publicly announced by [[Lucasfilm]] on [[February 6]], [[2018]] on [[StarWars.com]]. In the statement, Benioff and Weiss expressed how honored they felt to be working on the series, and Lucasfilm President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] praised their storytelling prowess.<ref name="New Film" />

On [[April 12]], [[2019]], during an interview with [[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']] at [[Celebration Chicago]], Kennedy mentioned that recently, she, Benioff, Weiss, and {{Film|VIII}} director [[Rian Johnson]] met to "lock down" their plans for their future ''Star Wars'' films.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/star-wars-disney-planning-decade-movies-rise-skywalker-1201761|text=Lucasfilm's Kathleen Kennedy on Planning "Next 10 Years" of Star Wars Films|author=Graeme McMillan|date=2019-04-12|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20190708170215}}</ref> In another Celebration interview with [[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']], Kennedy mentioned that Benioff and Weiss would be "working very closely" with Johnson. Additionally, Kennedy mentioned that the future slate of ''Star Wars'' films, including entries in this film series, could be set far in the past or far in the future with relation to the [[Star Wars saga|Skywalker saga]].<ref name="EW KK">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/movies/2019/04/13/lucasfilm-star-wars-movies-hiatus|text=Lucasfilm putting the ''Star Wars'' movies 'on hiatus' after this year|author=[[Wikipedia:Anthony Breznican|Anthony Breznican]]|date=2019-04-13|work=[[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']]|archivedate=20200803105613}}</ref>

In the summer of 2019, Benioff and Weiss met with George Lucas in [[Wikipedia:Italy|Italy]] to research the film.<ref name="THR report">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/why-star-wars-didnt-work-game-thrones-duo-1250798|text=Divided Attention and Toxic Fandom: Why the 'Game of Thrones' Duo Bailed on 'Star Wars'|author=Lesley Goldber|date=2019-10-30|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20200523084713}}</ref> However, on [[October 28]], [[2019]], it was reported that Benioff and Weiss had exited the film series due to scheduling conflicts with an [[Wikipedia:Production company#Deals|overall deal]] the pair had signed with [[Netflix]]<ref name="No Films?" /> [[October 30|Two days later]], [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] reported that the plans Benioff and Weiss had for the film series involved the exploration of the origins of the [[Jedi]],<ref name="Variety GoT">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/features/star-wars-kathleen-kennedy-david-benioff-db-weiss-1203388611|text='Star Wars': Inside 'Game of Thrones' Creators' Exit and the Pressures Facing Lucasfilm (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Brent Lang|date=2019-10-30|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200721105505}}</ref> a concept that later was announced to be at the center of [[James Mangold]]'s forthcoming [[Untitled Star Wars film (James Mangold)|''Star Wars'' film]].<ref name="New movies">{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-new-star-wars-films|text=SWCE 2023: Three New ''Star Wars'' Movies Announced|date=2023-04-07|quote=James Mangold's movie will go back to the dawn of the Jedi.}}</ref> ''The Hollywood Reporter'' disputed the claims that Benioff and Weiss departed solely due to scheduling conflicts and instead saying that Kennedy was "said to have been unhappy with the Netflix deal" and was not convinced the duo "could develop a sci-fi trilogy while also overseeing film and TV projects at Netflix." Additionally, they claimed that the pair's departure from the series happened around [[August]] of 2019.<ref name="THR report" />

Officially, Lucasfilm never commented on Benioff and Weiss's departure, though the original press release for the film series was removed from [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="New Film" /> On [[January 10]], [[2024]], Benioff and Weiss revealed that their ''Star Wars'' project, beginning with ''[[The First Jedi]]'', was focused on exploring how the [[Jedi Order]] began, why it began, and exploring the first [[lightsaber]]. Benioff and Weiss confirmed that Lucasfilm ultimately passed on the project and were not interested. Despite this, a [[Untitled Star Wars film (James Mangold)|''Star Wars'' film]] by [[James Mangold]] is set to explore the [[Timeline of galactic history#Dawn of the Jedi (c. 25,025 BBY)|dawn of the Jedi]].<ref name="THR 3BP" />

==Release and reception==
{{Quote|The conclusion that we reached was three years was the proper amount of time to not only take a breather and reset, but to really gear up for the next films released.|Disney CEO [[Bob Iger (chief executive officer)|Bob Iger]]|<ref name="Gizmodo">{{WebCite|url=https://gizmodo.com/the-first-star-wars-films-after-rise-of-skywalker-will-1834749699|text=It's Official: The First ''Star Wars'' Film After ''Rise of Skywalker'' Will Be From Game of Thrones' Showrunners|author=Beth Elderkin|date=2019-05-14|work=[[Wikipedia:Gizmodo|''Gizmodo'']]|archivedate=20210612212947}}</ref>}}
In [[September]] 2018, Bob Iger said that there would be a "slowdown" on the release of ''Star Wars'' films, because he felt there had been "a little too much, too fast."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/bob-iger-disneys-streaming-service-james-gunn-star-wars-slowdown-1145493|text=Bob Iger Talks Disney's Streaming Service, 'Roseanne,' James Gunn and a Coming 'Star Wars' "Slowdown"|author=Matthew Belloni|date=2018-09-20|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20200511001454}}</ref> 

On [[May 7]], 2019, Disney released its 2020–2027 theatrical release schedule, with a ''Star Wars'' film scheduled for [[December 16]], [[2022]].<ref name="Variety Disney 2019">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/disney-avatar-star-wars-marvel-1203207661|text=Disney Moves 'Avatar' Sequels, Announces New 'Star Wars' Films|author=Brent Lang and Rebecca Rubin|date=2019-05-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200727083136}}</ref> ''[[The Star Wars Show]]'' also reported on the news on [[May 15]].<ref name="SW Show">{{StarWarsShow|dUSoopV7EKo|Star Wars Dates Announced, Plus We Won an Emmy!|sw_url=video/star-wars-dates-announced-plus-we-won-an-emmy}}</ref> On [[May 14]], Iger confirmed that Benioff and Weiss's first film would take this release slot.<ref name="Gizmodo" />

After the pair's departure from the project, the release slot stayed on Disney's calendar and was delayed to [[December 22]], [[2023]] after the onset of the [[Wikipedia:COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Variety 2020">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/box-office/star-wars-films-avatar-sequels-pushed-back-a-year-in-disney-release-calendar-shakeup-1234715104|text='Star Wars' Films, 'Avatar' Sequels Pushed Back a Year in Disney Release Calendar Shakeup|author=Rebecca Rubin|date=2020-07-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200723212010}}</ref> On [[December 10]], [[2020]], 
Lucasfilm revealed that the release slot was given to the film [[Rogue Squadron (film)|''Rogue Squadron'']].<ref name="Announcement">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref> Lucasfilm ultimately passed on the project helmed by Benioff and Weiss.<ref name="THR 3BP" />
